sources.note: Main history, family principalities and ending. Entry typo545/1062 not repeated; Fars ending compressed as early1060s since exact sequence differs from other scholarship.

sources.title: Bürgel and Mottahedeh: Adud al-Dawla
sources.note: Direct scholarly article, Arabic learning/library paragraphs and building/festival paragraphs. Contemporary Muqaddasi and Biruni accounts explicitly attributed in public text.

sources.title: Judith A. Lerner: Band-e Amir in Iran
sources.note: Contemporary accounts, physical construction and later repairs. Erroneous calendar equivalence356/975 avoided; only tenth century. Irrigation counts are medieval reports, not modern measurements.

sources.title: Ashmolean Museum: Buyid silver dirham HCR14387
sources.note: Direct object catalogue, Arabic reverse field and English translation; Fasā,348AH/959 to 960,2.91g,25.7mm. Sample الامير العدل exactly from reverse, translated the Just Amir.

sources.title: D. M. Dunlop: Ibn Marzuban, Buyid hospital administrator
sources.note: Full scholarly biography;982 foundation, religious-law/sciences education, hospital superintendence and uncertainty over clinical role.

sources.title: US National Library of Medicine: al-Majusi’s Complete Book of the Medical Art
sources.note: Institutional manuscript catalogue: patron Adud, organization/anatomy/surgery, MS A26.1 copied1208. Do not assign surviving later copy to Buyid period.

sources.title: Paul Kunitzsch: Abd al-Rahman al-Sufi
sources.note: Scholarly biography, Buyid patronage, own observations and coordinates epoch1October964, illustrated classical/Arabic constellation traditions. Avoid disputed1009 Bodleian manuscript dating.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Shiites of Iraq
sources.note: Buyid patronage, Baghdad Karkh scholars, Sabur library991 to 992, Abbasid suzerainty and communal tensions. No universal religious identity inferred.

sources.title: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art: gold ewer F1943.1
sources.note: Direct museum catalogue:966 to 977 object field versus patron reign967 to 978; public date broad tenth century. Inscription apparently genuine, later handle, authenticity debate and reported provenance qualified.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: disputed Buyid silk, 30.67
sources.note: Direct museum catalogue:probably early20thcentury. Radiocarbon dates refer to related cloth in Abegg Foundation, not direct testing of Met piece. Actual1924excavations produced12thcentury shrouds, not Buyid clothes.
